title: The Fourier–Deligne transform
summary: Kernel transforms, trace functions, Lang-torsor character sheaves (Artin–Schreier and Kummer), and the ℓ-adic Fourier–Deligne transform on vector bundles over 𝔽_p-schemes: FT_! = FT_*, inversion, duality, functoriality, Plancherel, trace identity and Frobenius exchange, perverse t-exactness, and on the affine line the types of simple perverse sheaves, Fourier sheaves, the Kummer/Gauss-sum transform, Laumon's local monodromy and the local Fourier transforms with their tame values.

layers.title: Additive characters and the finite Fourier transform

targets.name: AddChar.IsNondegenerate
targets.statement: An additive character ψ : 𝔽_p → Λ^× of a commutative ring Λ is nondegenerate when ψ(1) − 1 is a unit of Λ.

api.name: IsNondegenerate.sub_one_isUnit
api.statement: ψ(a) − 1 is a unit for every a ∈ 𝔽_p^×.

api.name: IsNondegenerate.isUnit_p
api.statement: p is a unit of Λ and Φ_p(ψ(1)) = 0.

api.name: IsNondegenerate.inv
api.statement: ψ^{−1} and a ↦ ψ(c a), c ∈ 𝔽_p^×, are nondegenerate.

api.name: IsNondegenerate.map
api.statement: For a ring map h : Λ → Λ', h ∘ ψ is nondegenerate.

api.name: isNondegenerate_iff_forall_maximal
api.statement: For finite Λ, ψ is nondegenerate iff its reduction modulo every maximal ideal is nontrivial.

api.name: IsNondegenerate.isPrimitive
api.statement: For nonzero Λ, a nondegenerate character is AddChar.IsPrimitive (ψ(a) − 1 a unit, hence ψ(a) ≠ 1, for a ≠ 0).

tests.name: nondeg_product_nonexample
tests.statement: Λ = ℤ/7 × ℤ/7, ψ(1) = (2, 1): nontrivial but ψ(1) − 1 = (1, 0) is not a unit and Σψ = (0, 3) ≠ 0.

tests.name: nondeg_none_Z5
tests.statement: Λ = ℤ/5, p = 3: (ℤ/5)^× has no element of order 3, so no nondegenerate character exists.

tests.name: nondeg_zero_ring
tests.statement: Λ = 0: ψ(1) − 1 = 0 is a unit, so the unique character is nondegenerate, but it is trivial and not AddChar.IsPrimitive; the primitivity clause needs Λ ≠ 0.

targets.name: AddChar.IsNondegenerate.sum_trace_mul_eq_ite
targets.statement: For a nondegenerate ψ, a finite field k of characteristic p and y ∈ k, Σ_{x ∈ k} ψ(Tr_{k/𝔽_p}(x y)) = |k| if y = 0 and 0 otherwise; when Spec Λ is connected (in particular nonempty), every additive character of k into Λ^× is x ↦ ψ(Tr(c x)) for a unique c ∈ k.
hypotheses: k finite field of characteristic p

locator.where: Appendice (2.4), KL85 lines 442–446 (nontriviality of ψ in the local case); LAU87 (0.2), LAU87 lines 144–149, for the classification of ℚ̄_ℓ-valued characters of 𝔽_q; the orthogonality over a general commutative ring is this roadmap's own, proved by multiplying by ψ(Tr(x_0 y)) − 1

targets.name: finiteFourier
targets.statement: For a finite-dimensional vector space W over a finite field k of characteristic p, Λ and nondegenerate ψ, 𝔉_ψ : (W → Λ) → (Module.Dual k W → Λ), (𝔉_ψ t)(w') = Σ_{w ∈ W} t(w) ψ(Tr_{k/𝔽_p} w'(w)).

api.name: finiteFourier_linear
api.statement: 𝔉_ψ is Λ-linear.

api.name: finiteFourier_indicator_zero
api.statement: 𝔉_ψ of the indicator of 0 is the constant 1; of the constant 1 is |W| times the indicator of 0.

api.name: finiteFourier_indicator_subspace
api.statement: 𝔉_ψ of the indicator of a subspace U is |U| times the indicator of U^⊥.

api.name: finiteFourier_baseChange
api.statement: For k ⊂ k', 𝔉 on W ⊗ k' uses ψ ∘ Tr_{k'/𝔽_p}.

api.name: finiteFourier_eq_dft
api.statement: For Λ = ℂ, k = 𝔽_p, W = ZMod p, ψ = ZMod.stdAddChar: 𝔉_ψ Φ (k) = ZMod.dft Φ (−k).

tests.name: ff_zero_space
tests.statement: W = 0: 𝔉_ψ is the identity and |W| = 1.

tests.name: ff_degenerate_nonexample
tests.statement: With ψ(1) = (2,1) into ℤ/7 × ℤ/7 the second component of 𝔉 is t ↦ Σ t, not injective for |W| > 1.

tests.name: ff_dft_sign
tests.statement: For N = p = 3 and Φ = 1_{1}: ZMod.dft Φ k = stdAddChar(−k) while 𝔉Φ(k) = stdAddChar(k).

tests.name: ff_subspace_code_orthogonality
tests.statement: W = 𝔽_3² with the dot product, Λ = ℤ/7, ψ(1) = 2, U = span(1, 1): 𝔉_ψ(1_U) is 3 on U^⊥ = {(0,0), (1,2), (2,1)} and 0 elsewhere, as Tau Ceti's Submodule.sum_addChar_dotProduct gives for C = U; at (1, 1) ∈ U ∖ U^⊥ the value is ψ(0) + ψ(2) + ψ(1) = 7 ≡ 0, not |U| = 3.

targets.name: finiteFourier_inversion
targets.statement: Inversion 𝔉^{W^∨}(𝔉^W t)(w) = |W| t(−w); Plancherel Σ_{w'} 𝔉t_1(w') 𝔉t_2(w') = |W| Σ_w t_1(w) t_2(−w); convolution 𝔉(t_1 * t_2) = 𝔉t_1 · 𝔉t_2; 𝔉(f_! t) = 𝔉(t) ∘ f^∨ for linear f; translation 𝔉(t(· − e)) = ψ(Tr(·(e))) 𝔉t; 𝔉_{ψ^{−1}} t = 𝔉_ψ t ∘ [−1].

targets.name: kernelTransform
targets.statement: For S qcqs, torsion Λ, X, Y separated finitely presented over S, 𝒦 ∈ D⁺(X ×_S Y, Λ) of finite Tor amplitude and a ∈ ℤ, Φ_𝒦 : D⁺(X, Λ) → D⁺(Y, Λ), Φ_𝒦(K) = Rp_{Y!}(p_X^*K ⊗^L 𝒦)[a], a triangulated functor.
hypotheses: X, Y separated finitely presented over S

locator.where: Proposition (1.2.2.9), LAU87 lines 472–474, and BRY86 Proposition 9.4 1), BRY86 lines 3449–3450 and 3460, for base change of the Fourier kernel, proved by proper base change; BRY86 Définition 9.1, BRY86 line 3394, for the Fourier kernel as the motivating instance; SGA 4 XVII 5.4.3 as recalled at LAU87 lines 459–461 for Künneth; kernel transforms at this generality are this roadmap's own

api.name: kernelTransform_map
api.statement: A morphism of kernels induces a natural transformation, and triangles of kernels give triangles of functors.

api.name: kernelTransform_graph
api.statement: The graph kernel (id, f)_!Λ gives Rf_!; the kernel (g, id)_!Λ gives g^*.

api.name: kernelTransform_tensor
api.statement: Tensoring the kernel by p_Y^*M gives Φ(−) ⊗^L M.

api.name: kernelTransform_baseChange_comp
api.statement: Base-change isomorphisms satisfy identity and composition laws.

tests.name: kt_identity
tests.statement: X = Y = S, 𝒦 = Λ_S, a = 0: Φ is the identity.

tests.name: kt_compact_vs_ordinary
tests.statement: S = Spec k̄, X = 𝔸¹_S, Y = S, 𝒦 = Λ: Φ(Λ) = Λ(−1)[−2], whereas Rp_{Y*} would give Λ.

tests.name: kt_tor_nonexample
tests.statement: Λ = ℤ/4, 𝒦 = ℤ/2 on a geometric point: Φ(ℤ/2) has cohomology ℤ/2 in all degrees ≤ 0 and leaves D⁺.

tests.name: kt_graph_closed
tests.statement: For i : {0} → 𝔸¹ the graph kernel sends Λ to i_*Λ and the transposed one sends Λ_{𝔸¹} to Λ.

targets.name: kernelTransform_baseChange
targets.statement: For g : S' → S, g_Y^* Φ_𝒦(K) ≅ Φ_{𝒦'}(g_X^* K) with 𝒦' the pullback of 𝒦; and the relative Künneth isomorphism R(f ×_S g)_!(K ⊠_S L) ≅ Rf_!K ⊠_S Rg_!L for L of finite Tor amplitude.
hypotheses: 𝒦, L of finite Tor amplitude

locator.where: Proposition (1.2.2.9), LAU87 lines 472–474, and BRY86 Proposition 9.4 1), BRY86 lines 3449–3450 and 3460 (base change of the Fourier kernel, by proper base change); SGA 4 XVII 5.4.3 as recalled at LAU87 lines 459–461 (Künneth)

targets.name: kernelComp
targets.statement: For 𝒦 ∈ D⁺(X ×_S Y) and 𝒦' ∈ D⁺(Y ×_S Z) of finite Tor amplitude, 𝒦' ∘ 𝒦 = Rp_{XZ!}(p_{XY}^*𝒦 ⊗^L p_{YZ}^*𝒦') with shift a + a', and the composition isomorphism c : Φ_{𝒦'} ∘ Φ_𝒦 ≅ Φ_{𝒦'∘𝒦}.

api.name: kernelComp_torAmplitude
api.statement: 𝒦' ∘ 𝒦 has finite Tor amplitude and commutes with base change.

api.name: kernelComp_graph
api.statement: 𝒦 ∘ Γ_g = (g × id)^*𝒦 and Γ_h ∘ 𝒦 = R(id × h)_!𝒦.

api.name: kernelComp_assoc_pentagon
api.statement: The associator of composite kernels satisfies the pentagon identity.

tests.name: kc_graphs
tests.statement: Graph kernels compose to the graph kernel of the composite and c is the composition isomorphism of EtaleCohomologyFoundations §0.8.

tests.name: kc_unit
tests.statement: For 𝒦 = Δ_!Λ the left unitor composed with c is the identity of Φ_{𝒦'}.

tests.name: kc_shift_sign
tests.statement: Φ_{Λ[1]} composed with itself is [2], with the Koszul sign of exchanging shifts.

targets.name: kernelComp_coherence
targets.statement: The composition isomorphisms are natural in both kernels, associative for three composable kernels (compatible with the associator of kernels), unital for Δ_!Λ on either side, and compatible with base change along every S' → S.

locator.where: lines 413–417 and 440–444, the proofs of (1.2.2.1) and (1.2.2.4), which compose a Fourier kernel with a Fourier or a graph kernel by proper base change and the projection formula; the coherence statements are this roadmap's own

targets.name: kernelTransform_ctf
targets.statement: For Noetherian S, finite Λ with characteristic invertible on S and 𝒦 ∈ Dᵇ_ctf(X ×_S Y), Φ_𝒦 preserves Dᵇ_ctf, 𝒦' ∘ 𝒦 ∈ Dᵇ_ctf, and Φ_𝒦 commutes with derived change of coefficients.
hypotheses: Λ finite, char Λ invertible on S

targets.name: traceFunction
targets.statement: For X separated of finite type over 𝔽_q, finite Λ of characteristic prime to p and K ∈ Dᵇ_ctf(X, Λ), t_{K,n}(x) = L(Frob_x, K_x̄), the Lefschetz number of geometric Frobenius on the perfect complex K_x̄, for x ∈ X(𝔽_{qⁿ}).
hypotheses: X separated finite type over 𝔽_q

api.name: traceFunction_triangle
api.statement: Additive in distinguished triangles; t_{K[1]} = −t_K.

api.name: traceFunction_tensor
api.statement: t_{K ⊗^L L} = t_K · t_L and t_{f^*K} = t_K ∘ f.

api.name: traceFunction_baseExtension
api.statement: Over X ⊗ 𝔽_{q^m}, the level-n trace function is t_{K, mn}.

tests.name: tf_point_twist
tests.statement: On Spec 𝔽_q, Λ(−1)[−2] has t = q and Λ[1] has t = −1; arithmetic Frobenius would give q^{−1}.

tests.name: tf_skyscraper_fubini
tests.statement: t_{i_*Λ} is the indicator of 0 and the Fubini sum over 𝔸¹ gives q = t_{RΓ_c}.

tests.name: tf_perfect_complex
tests.statement: K = [ℤ/4 —2→ ℤ/4] on a point: t = 0 although H⁰ = H¹ = ℤ/2, where a trace on cohomology is undefined.

targets.name: traceFunction_lowerShriek
targets.statement: t_{Rf_!K, n}(y) = Σ_{f(x) = y} t_{K,n}(x) for separated f of finite type; hence t_{Φ_𝒦K,n}(y) = (−1)^a Σ_x t_{K,n}(x) t_{𝒦,n}(x, y); with realization to O_E and E.

targets.name: langTorsor
targets.statement: For G smooth connected commutative of finite type over 𝔽_q with q-Frobenius F and A = G(𝔽_q), the Lang map L = F − id : G → G as a finite étale A-torsor for translation.
hypotheses: G smooth connected commutative finite type over 𝔽_q

api.name: langTorsor_natural
api.statement: For φ : G → G', L_{G'} ∘ φ = φ ∘ L_G, so pushout along φ|_A is pullback along φ.

api.name: langTorsor_norm
api.statement: Fⁿ − id = (F − id)(1 + ⋯ + F^{n−1}) maps the qⁿ-Lang torsor to the q-Lang torsor, inducing the norm.

api.name: norm_surjective
api.statement: The norm G(𝔽_{qⁿ}) → G(𝔽_q) is surjective.

api.name: langTorsor_frobenius
api.statement: L commutes with F.

tests.name: lang_Ga
tests.statement: G = 𝔾_a: L(t) = t^q − t, kernel 𝔽_q; q = 3, x = 1: arithmetic Frobenius sends t to t + 1.

tests.name: lang_Gm
tests.statement: G = 𝔾_m: L(t) = t^{q−1}, kernel μ_{q−1}.

tests.name: lang_disconnected
tests.statement: Constant ℤ/2: F = id and L = 0 is not surjective.

tests.name: lang_trivial
tests.statement: G = 0: L is the identity of a point.

targets.name: langTorsor_isTorsor
targets.statement: L is étale (dL = −id), surjective (its image is an open subgroup; RG2.3.7 on points) with kernel the constant group A, hence a finite étale A-torsor; for x ∈ G(𝔽_{qⁿ}), Frob_x acts on L^{−1}(x)(𝔽̄_q) by translation by −N(x).
hypotheses: G smooth connected commutative finite type over 𝔽_q

targets.name: characterSheaf
targets.statement: For χ : A → Λ^×, ℒ_χ is the torsor–character sheaf of the Lang torsor with χ^{−1}, i.e. the χ-isotypic part of L_*Λ for (a·s)(t) = s(t + a); ℒ_χ(f) = f^*ℒ_χ for f : X → G.

api.name: characterSheaf_lisse
api.statement: ℒ_χ is lisse of rank one with monodromy through A.

api.name: characterSheaf_rigid_mult
api.statement: Rigidification at 0 and m^*ℒ_χ ≅ pr_1^*ℒ_χ ⊗ pr_2^*ℒ_χ, compatible, associative and commutative.

api.name: characterSheaf_add
api.statement: ℒ_χ(f + g) ≅ ℒ_χ(f) ⊗ ℒ_χ(g).

api.name: characterSheaf_frobenius
api.statement: Canonical F^*ℒ_χ ≅ ℒ_χ.

api.name: characterSheaf_translate
api.statement: t_a^*ℒ_χ ≅ ℒ_χ ⊗ π^*(line with Frobenius χ(a)) for a ∈ A.

tests.name: cs_convention_F3
tests.statement: G = 𝔾_a over 𝔽_3, Λ = ℤ/7, ψ(1) = 2: Frob_1 acts by 2, not ψ(−1) = 4.

tests.name: cs_quadratic_kummer
tests.statement: G = 𝔾_m over 𝔽_5, Λ = ℤ/3, quadratic χ: the sheaf of t² = x, traces +1 at 1, 4 and −1 at 2, 3.

tests.name: cs_trivial
tests.statement: χ = 1: ℒ_1 constant, whereas L_*Λ has rank |A|.

targets.name: characterSheaf_trace
targets.statement: For x ∈ G(𝔽_{qⁿ}), Frob_x acts on ℒ_χ by χ(N_{𝔽_{qⁿ}/𝔽_q}(x)); t_{ℒ_χ(f), n} = χ ∘ N ∘ f.

targets.name: characterSheaf_cohomology_eq_zero
targets.statement: If the elements χ(a) − 1, a ∈ A, generate the unit ideal, then RΓ_c(G_{𝔽̄_q}, ℒ_χ) = 0 and RΓ(G_{𝔽̄_q}, ℒ_χ) = 0; hence Σ_{x ∈ G(𝔽_{qⁿ})} χ(N x) = 0.

targets.name: artinSchreierSheaf
targets.statement: For nondegenerate ψ : 𝔽_p → Λ^×, ℒ_ψ is the character sheaf of 𝔾_{a,𝔽_p}; for an 𝔽_p-scheme X and f ∈ Γ(X, O_X), ℒ_ψ(f) = f^*ℒ_ψ.

api.name: artinSchreierSheaf_add
api.statement: ℒ_ψ(f + g) ≅ ℒ_ψ(f) ⊗ ℒ_ψ(g); ℒ_ψ(0) ≅ Λ.

api.name: artinSchreierSheaf_smul
api.statement: ℒ_ψ(c f) ≅ ℒ_{ψ(c·)}(f) for c ∈ 𝔽_p.

api.name: artinSchreierSheaf_coboundary
api.statement: ℒ_ψ(f^p) ≅ ℒ_ψ(f) and ℒ_ψ(f^p − f) ≅ Λ.

api.name: artinSchreierSheaf_trace
api.statement: Over 𝔽_q: ℒ_ψ on 𝔾_{a,𝔽_q} is the character sheaf of ψ ∘ Tr; t(x) = ψ(Tr_{𝔽_{qⁿ}/𝔽_p} f(x)).

tests.name: as_zero_and_p
tests.statement: ℒ_ψ(0) = Λ; ℒ_ψ(x^p) ≅ ℒ_ψ(x) has Swan 1 at ∞, not p.

tests.name: as_coboundary_equal_traces
tests.statement: ℒ_ψ(x² − x) ≅ ℒ_ψ(x² − x³) on 𝔸¹_{𝔽_3}; traces agree on all 𝔽_{3ⁿ}.

targets.name: kummerSheaf
targets.statement: Over a field k with |μ_N(k)| = N, N invertible, for χ : μ_N(k) → Λ^×, ℒ_χ is the torsor–character sheaf of [N] : 𝔾_m → 𝔾_m with χ^{−1}; ℒ_χ(g) = g^*ℒ_χ for g ∈ Γ(X, O_X^×); over 𝔽_q with N = q − 1 it is the character sheaf of 𝔾_m.
hypotheses: N invertible in k with |μ_N(k)| = N

api.name: kummerSheaf_mul
api.statement: ℒ_χ(gh) ≅ ℒ_χ(g) ⊗ ℒ_χ(h); ℒ_χ ⊗ ℒ_χ' ≅ ℒ_{χχ'}; ℒ_1 ≅ Λ.

api.name: kummerSheaf_divisibility
api.statement: Compatibility with N | N' through ζ ↦ ζ^{N'/N}; [d]^*ℒ_χ ≅ ℒ_{χ^d}.

api.name: kummerSheaf_tame
api.statement: Tamely ramified at 0 and ∞ with inertia through the tame character.

api.name: kummerSheaf_jshriek
api.statement: If χ(ζ) − 1 is a unit, RΓ_c(𝔾_{m,k̄}, ℒ_χ) = 0 and j_!ℒ_χ ≅ Rj_*ℒ_χ.

tests.name: ks_F5
tests.statement: k = 𝔽_5, N = 4: the Kummer cover is the Lang torsor of 𝔾_m.

tests.name: ks_trivial_nonexample
tests.statement: Trivial χ: (Rj_*Λ)_0 has H⁰ = Λ and H¹ = Λ(−1), so j_!Λ ≠ Rj_*Λ.

tests.name: ks_complex_sign
tests.statement: k = ℂ, N = 2, Λ = ℤ/3, sign χ: χ(−1) − 1 = 1 is a unit and j_!ℒ_χ = Rj_*ℒ_χ.

targets.name: HenselianTrait.completion_ramification
targets.statement: For a henselian discrete valuation ring R with fraction field K and perfect residue field of characteristic p, and its completion K̂, restriction Gal(K̂^sep/K̂) → Gal(K^sep/K) is an isomorphism carrying inertia and wild inertia onto those of the trait Spec R and G_{K̂}^u onto G_K^u for every u ≥ 0 (upper numbering of G_K from the lower numbering on O_L for finite Galois L/K); breaks, break decompositions and Swan conductors of G_K-representations are those of ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations §3.1 through it. K̂/K need not be separable.
hypotheses: residue field perfect of characteristic p

locator.where: (2.1.1), LAU87 lines 680–688 (R between k{π} and k[[π]], ramification taken from the completion); proof by the finite étale equivalence and density of O_L in O_{L̂}

tests.name: completion_artinSchreier
tests.statement: R = k{π}, R̂ = k[[π]]: α^p − α = π^{−m}, p ∤ m, has upper jump m over k((π)) and hence over K.

tests.name: completion_nonExcellent
tests.statement: R the henselization of the valuation ring of k(π, f^p) ⊂ k((π)), f transcendental over k(π): K̂/K inseparable (f ∈ K̂), restriction still an isomorphism.

tests.name: completion_nonHenselian
tests.statement: R = k[π]_(π), p odd: K(√(1 + π)) splits over K̂, so restriction is not onto.

targets.name: artinSchreierSheaf_line
targets.statement: For k perfect of characteristic p, f ∈ k[x] of degree d ≥ 1 prime to p and ψ nondegenerate: ℒ_ψ(f) is lisse on 𝔸¹, totally wild at ∞ with single break d and Swan d; H⁰_c = H²_c = 0, H¹_c free of rank d − 1, H¹_c → H¹ an isomorphism; for lisse F with breaks < d at ∞ and field coefficients, F ⊗ ℒ_ψ(f) has all breaks d, H²_c = 0 and H¹_c of rank (d − 1) rank F.

layers.title: The Fourier–Deligne transform on a vector bundle

targets.name: fourierKernel
targets.statement: For S an 𝔽_p-scheme and E finite locally free of rank r, the pairing ⟨ , ⟩ : V(E) ×_S V(E^∨) → 𝔾_{a,S} (the identity of End E) and the kernel ℒ_ψ⟨ , ⟩ = ⟨ , ⟩^*ℒ_ψ.
hypotheses: E finite locally free of constant rank r

api.name: fourierKernel_add
api.statement: (s × id)^*ℒ_ψ⟨,⟩ ≅ p_13^*ℒ_ψ⟨,⟩ ⊗ p_23^*ℒ_ψ⟨,⟩, and symmetrically.

api.name: fourierKernel_transpose
api.statement: (f × id)^*ℒ_ψ⟨,⟩_2 ≅ (id × f^∨)^*ℒ_ψ⟨,⟩_1 for linear f.

api.name: fourierKernel_zero
api.statement: Restriction to σ(S) ×_S V' and V ×_S σ'(S) is Λ.

api.name: fourierKernel_baseChange
api.statement: Compatible with base change S' → S.

api.name: fourierKernel_bidual
api.statement: Under evalIso, the kernel of E^∨ is the transpose of that of E.

tests.name: fk_rank_one
tests.statement: E = O_S: the pairing is x x' on 𝔸²_S.

tests.name: fk_rank_zero
tests.statement: r = 0: V = V' = S and the kernel is Λ_S.

tests.name: fk_not_pullback
tests.statement: ℒ_ψ(x x') is not a pullback from either factor of 𝔸¹ × 𝔸¹.

targets.name: fourierDeligne
targets.statement: FT_ψ = FT_{ψ,!} : D⁺(V, Λ) → D⁺(V', Λ), FT_ψ(K) = Rpr'_!(pr^*K ⊗ ℒ_ψ⟨ , ⟩)[r], and FT_{ψ,*}(K) = Rpr'_*(pr^*K ⊗ ℒ_ψ⟨ , ⟩)[r] with the forget-supports map.

api.name: fourierDeligne_triangulated
api.statement: Triangulated; commutes with shifts and twists.

api.name: fourierDeligne_projection
api.statement: FT(K ⊗ π^*M) ≅ FT(K) ⊗ π'^*M for M of finite Tor amplitude.

api.name: fourierDeligne_eq_kernelTransform
api.statement: FT_ψ is the kernel transform with kernel ℒ_ψ⟨,⟩ and shift r.

tests.name: ft_rank_zero
tests.statement: r = 0: FT is the identity.

tests.name: ft_delta
tests.statement: On 𝔸¹_{𝔽_q}: FT(i_{0*}Λ) = Λ[1], trace −1 everywhere = −Σ δ_0(x)ψ(x x').

tests.name: ft_trivial_character
tests.statement: Trivial ψ: FT(K) = π'^*Rπ_!K[r].

targets.name: projective_line_ula_artinSchreier
targets.statement: The projection ℙ¹ ×_{𝔽_p} 𝔸¹ → ℙ¹ is universally locally acyclic relative to (j × 1)_!ℒ_ψ(x y), and the strict-local comparison maps stay isomorphisms after tensoring with any Λ-module.

locator.where: Théorème (2.4.4), KL85 lines 567–568; LAU87 Théorème (1.3.1.2), LAU87 lines 526–529

targets.name: fourierDeligne_lowerShriek_iso_lowerStar
targets.statement: For every qcqs 𝔽_p-scheme S, E and K ∈ D⁺(V, Λ), FT_{ψ,!}(K) → FT_{ψ,*}(K) is an isomorphism.

locator.where: Théorème (2.4.1), KL85 lines 447–449, proof lines 450–554; LAU87 Théorème (1.3.1.1), LAU87 lines 521–525

targets.name: fourierKernel_lowerShriek
targets.statement: Rpr_!ℒ_ψ⟨ , ⟩ ≅ σ_*Λ(−r)[−2r] on V, and FT_ψ(π^*M[r]) ≅ σ'_*M(−r) for M ∈ D⁺(S, Λ).

targets.name: fourierDeligne_inversion
targets.statement: The natural isomorphism ι_K : FT^{V'}_ψ(FT^V_ψ K) ≅ [−1]^*K(−r), compatible with base change; FT_ψ is an equivalence with quasi-inverse [−1]^*FT^{V'}_ψ(−)(r); Rπ'_!FT_ψ(K) ≅ σ^*K(−r)[−r] and σ'^*FT_ψ(K) ≅ Rπ_!K[r].

api.name: inversion_baseChange
api.statement: ι commutes with base change S' → S.

tests.name: inv_trivial_nonexample
tests.statement: Trivial ψ: FT(FT(i_{0*}Λ)) = Λ_{𝔸¹}(−1).

tests.name: inv_sign
tests.statement: FT(FT(i_{a*}Λ)) ≅ i_{(−a)*}Λ(−1); without [−1]^* the support would be a ≠ −a for p odd.

targets.name: fourierDeligne_duality
targets.statement: For S Noetherian, K ∈ Dᵇ_ctf(V) and M ∈ D⁺(S): RHom(FT_ψ K, π'^!M) ≅ FT_{ψ^{−1}}(RHom(K, π^!M))(r); D_{V'/S}FT_ψ ≅ FT_{ψ^{−1}} D_{V/S}(r); over a field D FT_ψ ≅ FT_{ψ^{−1}} D (r).

locator.where: Théorème (1.3.2.1), Corollaire (1.3.2.2), LAU87 lines 553–565; KL85 (2.1.5)(ii), KL85 lines 390–391

targets.name: fourierDeligne_functoriality
targets.statement: Base change g'^*FT ≅ FT g^* and FT Rg_{V!} ≅ Rg_{V'!} FT; for linear f : E_1 → E_2, FT(Rf_!K) ≅ f^{∨*}FT(K)[r_2 − r_1]; external products; FT(K_1 * K_2) ≅ FT K_1 ⊗ FT K_2[−r]; Plancherel Rπ'_!(FT K_1 ⊗ FT K_2) ≅ Rπ_!(K_1 ⊗ [−1]^*K_2)(−r); FT(Λ_{V(F)}[s]) ≅ Λ_{V(F^⊥)}(−s)[r − s]; FT(τ_{e*}K) ≅ FT(K) ⊗ ℒ_ψ⟨e, ·⟩; in every characteristic [2]^*FT(ℒ_ψ(q)) ≅ ℒ_ψ(−q') ⊗ π'^*Rπ_!ℒ_ψ(q)[r]; m^*K ≅ M ⊠ L induces m'^*FT(K) ≅ M ⊠ FT(L).

targets.name: fourierDeligne_coefficients
targets.statement: For Noetherian S, FT preserves Dᵇ_ctf; FT_{h∘ψ}(Λ' ⊗^L K) ≅ Λ' ⊗^L FT_ψ(K); for O_E the levelwise transform of a normalized system is normalized, and the E, ℚ̄_ℓ transforms are realizations, with §§3.3–3.6 transported.

targets.name: fourierDeligne_traceFunction
targets.statement: For S separated of finite type over 𝔽_q and K ∈ Dᵇ_ctf(V): t_{FT K, n}(e') = (−1)^r Σ_{e ∈ V_s(𝔽_{qⁿ})} t_{K,n}(e) ψ(Tr⟨e, e'⟩), with the trace forms of inversion, convolution and Plancherel.
hypotheses: S separated finite type over 𝔽_q

targets.name: fourierDeligne_frobeniusExchange
targets.statement: For S = S_0 ⊗ 𝔽̄_q and F = F_{V_0} × id, a canonical natural isomorphism F^*FT_ψ(K) ≅ FT_ψ(F^*K), compatible with powers of F and base change, so FT carries pairs (K, φ : F^*K ≅ K) to such pairs, recovering the descent datum of FT(K_0) for descended K.

api.name: frobExchange_comp
api.statement: Compatible with composition F^{m+n} = F^m F^n.

api.name: frobExchange_descended
api.statement: For K = K_0 descended, the induced structure is the descent datum of FT(K_0).

tests.name: fe_point
tests.statement: S_0 = Spec 𝔽_q, r = 0: the exchange is the identity.

tests.name: fe_trace
tests.statement: r = 1, K = Λ_{𝔸¹}: the transported Frobenius on FT(K)_{0'} = Λ(−1)[−1] has trace −q.

tests.name: fe_moves_points
tests.statement: S_0 = 𝔸¹: F moves points of S, so the exchange is not the identity on underlying complexes.

targets.name: fourierDeligne_tExact
targets.statement: Over a field k of characteristic p, FT_ψ : Dᵇ_c(V) → Dᵇ_c(V') is t-exact for the middle perversity (finite Λ with nondegenerate ψ, O_E, E, ℚ̄_ℓ), and for O_E also for p⁺.

locator.where: Théorème (1.3.2.3), LAU87 lines 566–575; KL85 (2.1.5)(iii), KL85 lines 392–393

targets.name: fourierDeligne_pervEquiv
targets.statement: FT_ψ restricts to an equivalence Perv(V) → Perv(V') with quasi-inverse [−1]^*FT^{V'}_ψ(−)(r), on both hearts for O_E, compatible with duality, sending simple objects to simple objects for field coefficients.

layers.title: The transform on the affine line

targets.name: perverseLocalInvariants
targets.statement: For perverse K on a smooth connected curve X and a closed point x: rk(K) the rank of H^{−1}(K) at the generic point, rk_x(K) = dim H^{−1}(K_x̄) − dim H⁰(K_x̄), sw_x(K) Swan conductor of H^{−1}(K_{η̄_x}) (through 2.7.1), a_x(K) = rk(K) + sw_x(K) − rk_x(K).
hypotheses: X smooth connected curve over k

api.name: localInvariants_additive
api.statement: rk, rk_x, sw_x, a_x are additive on short exact sequences of perverse sheaves.

api.name: localInvariants_baseExtension
api.statement: For finite k'/k inside k̄ and a connected component X' of X ⊗ k', the pullback of K has generic rank rk(K) and the same rk_x, sw_x, a_x at points over x.

api.name: localInvariants_middle
api.statement: For j_{!*}F[1]: a_x = 0 on U and rk_x = dim F^{I_x} off U.

tests.name: li_skyscraper
tests.statement: i_{x*}Λ on ℙ¹: rk = 0, rk_x = −1, a_x = 1, χ = 1 = 1 − 2·0; the unsigned formula would give −1.

tests.name: li_disconnected_nonexample
tests.statement: X = ℙ¹ ⊔ ℙ¹, K = Λ[1] ⊔ 0: χ = −2 but the right side is −4 or 0; X = ℙ¹_{𝔽_{q²}} over 𝔽_q (C = 2, g = 0), K = Λ[1]: −4 on both sides.

targets.name: perverseLocalInvariants_eulerPoincare
targets.statement: a_x(K) ≥ rk(K) − rk_x(K) ≥ 0, with a_x(K) = 0 iff K[−1] is lisse at x iff rk_x(K) = rk(K); for X projective χ(X_{k̄}, K) = Σ_x deg(x) a_x(K) − χ(X_{k̄}) rk(K), χ(X_{k̄}) = C(2 − 2g) with C the number of components of X_{k̄} and g their common genus.
hypotheses: X smooth connected curve over perfect k

targets.name: swan_tensor_slopeOne
targets.statement: Slope decomposition and s(V) = Σ λ r(V_λ); for L of rank one and Swan one, s(V ⊗ L) = r(V_{[0,1[}) + s(V_1 ⊗ L) + s(V_{]1,∞[}) with s(V_1 ⊗ L) ≤ r(V_1); ℒ_ψ(a/π) has slope one; for k algebraically closed and V ≠ 0 purely of slope one, some a ∈ k makes V ⊗ ℒ_ψ(a/π) have a nonzero part of slope < 1. Route of the last clause, with K = k((π)) and G^u the upper ramification subgroups of G_K: G^1/G^{1+} is abelian of exponent p, so it suffices that every character θ of it is ℒ_ψ(b/π)|_{G^1} for some b ∈ k. θ factors through H^1 = Gal(L/L_0) for a finite Galois L/K with group H, H^{1+} = 1 and L_0 = L^{H^1}; with m = ψ_{L_0/K}(1) (Herbrand function), G^1 = G_{L_0}^m and G^{1+} = G_{L_0}^{m+}, so θ = ℒ_ψ(w) for a class w ∈ L_0/℘(L_0) of break ≤ m. In L_0 = k((ϖ_0)), every class has a representative that is integral or of pole order prime to p, two representatives with poles of order prime to p have the same pole order, and such a pole makes the class nontrivial (pinned Tau Ceti statements at the ϖ_0-adic place), and the termwise reduced representative is the roadmap's own; the coefficient c(b) of ϖ_0^{−m} in the reduced representative of the class of b/π is injective and additive in b, with c(b)^{p^N} an additive polynomial in b, hence a monomial and onto k; choosing c(b) equal to the coefficient of w leaves w − [b/π] of break < m, trivial on G_{L_0}^m = G^1.
hypotheses: henselian trait of equal characteristic p, perfect residue field (no excellence assumed)

tests.name: twist_slopeHalf_untwist
tests.statement: k = 𝔽̄_p, W of rank 2 purely of slope 1/2, b ≠ 0: V = W ⊗ ℒ_ψ(b/π) is purely of slope one and a = −b returns W, of slope 1/2.

tests.name: twist_nonClosed_nonexample
tests.statement: k = 𝔽_p, c ∈ 𝔽_{p²} ∖ 𝔽_p, V induced from ℒ_ψ(c/π) on the unramified quadratic extension: purely of slope one, and for every a ∈ 𝔽_p both characters ℒ_ψ((c + a)/π), ℒ_ψ((c^p + a)/π) of V ⊗ ℒ_ψ(a/π) have slope one; algebraic closure of k is needed.

tests.name: artinSchreier_reduced_poleOrder
tests.statement: k = 𝔽̄_3, L_0 = k((t)), u = t^{−6} + t^{−4} + t^{−2} (pole order 6): w = t^{−2} gives the reduced t^{−4} + 2t^{−2}; z = t^{−2} + t^{−1} gives t^{−4} − t^{−3} + 2t^{−2} + t^{−1}, pole order 4 again, reducing to t^{−4} + 2t^{−2}; break 4, not the naive 6.

targets.name: simplePerverse_types_fourier
targets.statement: Every simple perverse sheaf on A is of exactly one type (T1) i_{s*}F, (T2) (pr_A)_*(ℒ_ψ(x s') ⊗ pr_{s'}^*F')[1], (T3) j_{!*}F[1] with no geometric subquotient ℒ_ψ(x a'); FT exchanges (T1) and (T2'), (T3) and (T3'), with FT(i_{s*}F) ≅ (pr_{A'})_*(ℒ_ψ(s x') ⊗ pr_s^*F)[1] and FT of (T2) at s' ≅ [−1]^*i'_{s'*}F'(−1).

targets.name: fourierSheaf
targets.statement: Elementary sheaves (H⁰_c = 0, H²_c(ℱ ⊗ ℒ_ψ(t x)) = 0 for all t), Fourier sheaves (middle extension, H⁰ = H²_c = 0 after every twist ℒ_ψ(t x)), irreducible Fourier sheaves, and NFT_ψ(ℱ) = R¹pr'_!(pr^*ℱ ⊗ ℒ_ψ(x x')).

api.name: fourierSheaf_dual
api.statement: Middle-extension duals, translates and twists by ℒ_ψ(a x) of Fourier sheaves are Fourier.

api.name: fourierSheaf_nft
api.statement: For Fourier ℱ, NFT(ℱ) is the only cohomology sheaf of FT(ℱ[1])[−1], with stalk H¹_c(ℱ ⊗ ℒ_ψ(a x)) at a.

api.name: fourierSheaf_typeT3
api.statement: ℱ irreducible Fourier ⇒ ℱ[1] simple of type (T3); over k̄ conversely.

tests.name: fs_constant_nonexample
tests.statement: Λ_{𝔸¹} is not elementary (H²_c ≠ 0 at t = 0); ℒ_ψ(x) is neither elementary nor Fourier (t = −1); j_!(ℒ_χ|_{𝔸¹ ∖ {0,1}}) for nontrivial Kummer χ is elementary but not Fourier (stalk 0 at 1 against Λ for j_*j^*).

tests.name: fs_quadratic
tests.statement: ℒ_ψ(x²), p odd: Fourier, NFT = ℒ_ψ(−x'²/4) ⊗ H¹_c line.

tests.name: fs_kummer
tests.statement: j_!ℒ_χ: Fourier with NFT = j'_!ℒ_{χ^{−1}} ⊗ G(χ, ψ), generic rank 1 = a_0.

targets.name: naiveFourier_fourierSheaf
targets.statement: For elementary ℱ: FT(ℱ[1]) ≅ NFT(ℱ)[1], NFT(ℱ) elementary, NFT(NFT ℱ) ≅ [−1]^*ℱ(−1); Fourier ↦ Fourier with D NFT(ℱ) ≅ NFT([−1]^*Dℱ)(1); irreducible Fourier ↦ irreducible Fourier; over 𝔽_q, t_{NFT ℱ} = −𝔉_ψ(t_ℱ).

targets.name: gaussSumLine
targets.statement: G(χ, ψ) = H¹_c(𝔾_{m,k̄}, ℒ_χ ⊗ ℒ_ψ(x)) with its Gal(k̄/k)-action, for χ a character of μ_N(k) with χ(ζ) − 1 a unit.

api.name: gaussSumLine_baseChange
api.statement: Commutes with extension of k and is functorial in Λ.

tests.name: gs_product
tests.statement: G(χ,ψ) ⊗ G(χ^{−1},ψ) has Frobenius χ(−1) q, matching gaussSum_mul_gaussSum_eq_card and mul_gaussSum_inv_eq_gaussSum.

tests.name: gs_F5_F11
tests.statement: q = 5, Λ = 𝔽_11, ψ(1) = 3, quadratic χ: g ≡ 4 and g² ≡ 5 = χ(−1)·5.

targets.name: fourierDeligne_kummer
targets.statement: H^i_c(𝔾_{m,k̄}, ℒ_χ ⊗ ℒ_ψ(x)) = 0 for i ≠ 1, G(χ, ψ) has rank one, over 𝔽_q Frob acts on it by −Σ_{x ∈ 𝔽_q^×} χ(x)ψ(Tr x), and FT(j_!ℒ_χ[1]) ≅ j'_!ℒ_{χ^{−1}}[1] ⊗ G(χ, ψ).

targets.name: fourierDeligne_localMonodromy
targets.statement: For perverse K on A with K' = FT(K): rk(K') = Σ_s deg(s)a_s(K) + s(F_{∞,]1,∞[}) − r(F_{∞,]1,∞[}); rk_{s'}(K') = rk(K') − r(F_{∞,1}) + s(F_{∞,1} ⊗ ℒ_ψ(x s')) for s' ≠ 0'; rk_{0'}(K') = rk(K') − r(F_{∞,[0,1[}) + s(F_{∞,[0,1[}); the lisse-locus criterion; vanishing cycles at finite s' and at ∞'; the exact sequence 0 → H⁰_c(A_{k̄}, K) → F'_{η̄_{0'}} → R^{−1}Φ_{0'}(K') → H¹_c(A_{k̄}, K) → 0.

targets.name: naiveFourier_wildLisse_equiv
targets.statement: NFT_ψ restricts to an autoequivalence of the category of lisse sheaves on A all of whose breaks at ∞ exceed 1, with quasi-inverse [−1]^*NFT_ψ(−)(1).

targets.name: localFourierTransform
targets.statement: For henselian traits T, T' of equal characteristic p with residue field k and uniformizers π, π', the functors 𝔉^{(0,∞')}, 𝔉^{(∞,0')}, 𝔉^{(∞,∞')} : 𝒢 → 𝒢' given by the vanishing cycles for pr' : T ×_k T' → T' of pr^*(V_!) ⊗ ℒ_ψ(π/π'), ⊗ ℒ_ψ(π'/π), ⊗ ℒ_ψ(1/(ππ')) at the point over (t, η̄'), with 𝔉(V) the degree-one cohomology.
hypotheses: T, T' henselian traits over k with residue field k (not necessarily excellent)

api.name: localFourier_triangulated
api.statement: Triangulated at the level of complexes; commutes with unramified twists.

api.name: localFourier_baseChange
api.statement: Commutes with extension of k and change of Λ.

api.name: localFourier_scale
api.statement: ψ ↦ ψ(c·) composes with π' ↦ c^{−1}π' for (0,∞'), (∞,∞') and π' ↦ cπ' for (∞,0').

tests.name: lf_kummer_0inf
tests.statement: 𝔉^{(0,∞')}(V_χ) = V'_χ ⊗ G(χ, ψ); χ^{−1} would contradict the trace witness of 5.4.

tests.name: lf_infinf_tame_zero
tests.statement: 𝔉^{(∞,∞')} vanishes on tame modules.

targets.name: localFourierTransform_globalComparison
targets.statement: Comparison with global vanishing cycles (shift 2) for K ≅ V_![1] near 0 or ≅ V[1] near ∞, in particular R^{−1}Φ_{0'}(K') ≅ 𝔉^{(∞,0')}(F_∞) in the sequence at 0' of 5.5; concentration in degree 1 for V that are local monodromies of perverse sheaves on A, hence for all tame V when k is finite; compatibility with extension of k.
hypotheses: T, T' henselian traits over k with residue field k (not necessarily excellent)

locator.where: Lemme (2.4.2.1), Proposition (2.4.2.2), (2.5.2), LAU87 lines 1063–1090 and 1157–1165; Proposition (2.3.2.1)(iii), LAU87 lines 993–995

suppliers.what: compactifications and Rf_!, base change, local acyclicity, Künneth and projection formula on Noetherian bases, finiteness, traits and tame character, adic realization, f^! and duality, smooth purity and trace, field perverse t-structure, Frobenius and perfect-complex traces
enhancement, tensor–Hom and coherent derived functors
scheme Frobenius; 𝔾_a, 𝔾_m, μ_n; Kummer and Artin–Schreier sequences, finite pushforward
relative Spec, geometric vector bundles and duals
finite étale algebras unchanged under henselian completion, for the Galois group of a henselian trait and its completion
lower ramification groups and their graded pieces, the absolute upper filtration, ψ_{L/K} and the open-subgroup identity G_K^u ∩ G_L = G_L^{ψ_{L/K}(u)}, for the slope-one twisting lemma
breaks, Swan conductors, Artin–Schreier characters over complete fields (transported to henselian traits by 2.7.1)

consumers.what: can import artinSchreierSheaf, kummerSheaf with their traces and the Gauss-sum line (§§2.3, 2.5–2.6, 5.4) for the trace-function reading of its §3.6, background there, which names ℒ_ψ, ℒ_χ with the normalization ψ(Tr x), χ(N x) and the eigenvalue −g(χ, ψ)

can import kernel transforms and the composition coherence of kernels (§§1.1–1.2); it builds its convolution Ra_!(K ⊠ L) and its coherence from EtaleCohomologyFoundations §0.8 and describes convolution as the transform with the difference kernel

gaps.title: Rank-one lisse sheaves from finite étale torsors and characters
gaps.detail: For a finite étale A-torsor P → X under a finite group A and χ : A → Λ^×, the sheaf P ×^A Λ(χ) with its isotypic-part description, monodromy through lisseMonodromyEquiv, tensor compatibility, functoriality in A, pullback and coefficient change, with no invertibility of |A|.
gaps.needs: The contracted-product construction of a rank-one lisse sheaf from a finite étale torsor and a character, with its basic API.
gaps.section: §F.0.3 (rank-one lisse sheaves from torsors and characters)

gaps.title: Projection formula for Rf_! on D⁺ over qcqs bases
gaps.detail: For separated finitely presented f between qcqs schemes and torsion Λ, Rf_!(B ⊗^L f^*A) ≅ Rf_!B ⊗^L A for A ∈ D⁺(Y), B ∈ D⁺(X) with one of them of finite Tor amplitude, natural and compatible with composition and base change. On Noetherian bases for Dᵇ_ctf objects this is §F.2.7.
gaps.needs: The compact-support projection formula on bounded-below torsion complexes over qcqs bases with one factor of finite Tor amplitude.
gaps.section: §0.8 and §F.5 (projection formula of the six-operation structure)

gaps.title: Exceptional pullback and internal Hom under smooth morphisms over Noetherian bases
gaps.detail: For smooth separated finitely presented f of relative dimension d between Noetherian schemes with char Λ invertible: f^!M ≅ f^*M(d)[2d] for M ∈ D⁺(Y), and f^*RHom(K, M) ≅ RHom(f^*K, f^*M) for K ∈ Dᵇ_c(Y). Over separated finite-type schemes over a field this is EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves §2.7.
gaps.needs: Smooth purity for an arbitrary bounded-below complex and smooth base change for internal Hom with constructible source, over Noetherian bases.
